history.claim_summary: Agri-SCHOLAR issues weekly in-season irrigation and fertilizer advisories in which LLM agents set agronomically feasible action bounds and an optimizer searches within them, scoring each candidate with APSIM on a weather trajectory restricted to information available at the decision date.
history.evaluation_summary: Eleven kharif maize seasons (2015-2025) in one irrigated and one rainfed South Asian region with ERA5 daily weather; weekly advisories are replayed in APSIM under realized weather and compared with the regional package of practices on yield, net profit, production cost and sustainability penalty, with loose-bound and no-bound ablations of the bounding agent (Gemma-4-E4B-it agents).
corrections: All outcomes are APSIM simulations (the simulator is not calibrated against field trials) and the seven-day forecast is a synthetic perturbation of observed weather, so the gains do not establish field yields or performance with operational forecasts.

In the irrigated-region ablation, loose expert-range bounds give higher mean yield and profit than the LLM bounds; the demonstrated benefit of the LLM bounding agent is a lower sustainability penalty and agronomically practical doses, not higher profit.

citation.title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
citation.authors: Shen, ChengAo and Zhao, Yanjun and Liu, Haoxin and Chen, Bonnie and Ma, Miles and Song, Dongjin and Tong, Hanghang and Wen, Qingsong and He, Jingrui and Ni, Jingchao

claim.summary: TSFLab contributes an agent-agnostic workbench that provides forecasting research guidance, structured temporal knowledge, shared experiment execution, and verified maintenance of reusable research resources.
claim.evidence_basis: terra_reaudit_20261107: PDF p.1; source text L22

evidence.quote: propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic “workbench” that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources.

process_validity.quote: A session is accepted if it covers the complete requested matrix with executed metrics, the prescribed splits, train-only scaling, the common evaluation over all windows, and no test-informed configuration selection;

temporal_validity.quote: Data. Chronological 70/10/20 split; train-only scaling; all channels; input 168 and horizon 24.

task_performance.quote: On ETTh1 and Weather (Fig. 3b,c), TSFLab reaches the lowest test MSE with less time and fewer fresh tokens than every other setting; details are in App. D.

automation_evidence.quote:
Paper reproduction: the agent reproduces the reported results of a recent forecasting
paper that has no official code

metric_evidence.quote:
TSFLab reproduces 73% of the 96 scheduled results
within 10% of the paper’s MSE, against 21–46% for the other settings.

evidence.quote:
Without the Experiment Workflower, agents write their own training and evaluation code; they
add the most code, and their errors move into evaluation, such as tuning on test scores and averaging batch
errors.

practical_problems.note: module ablation (with the guide ablation, whose rejected attempts used wrong ETTh1 split boundaries) shows that without shared splitting and execution agents tune on test scores; reported qualitatively as error types, not as a leakage-rate measurement

task_impact.summary: Automates forecasting reproduction, benchmarking and method development for coding agents through a shared workbench with fixed chronological protocols; it raises task completion and reproduction fidelity and cuts tokens, and its module ablations qualitatively show protocol errors such as test-score tuning when the shared runner or guide is removed.

source_evidence.quote: propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic “workbench” that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources.

For example, when benchmarking methods on a new dataset, a skill guides the agent to identify time fields, forecasting variables, sampling frequency, and evaluation settings, then register data through the workbench’s “add” interface and inspect partitioning and scaling through its “split” interface.

It provides a knowledge card for each method, dataset, and unit, organized into summary, card, and source levels. Summaries support screening; cards describe capabilities, parameters, interfaces, and limitations; sources provide papers, reference code, and detailed explanations.

Knowledge Structurer also extracts common blocks, such as RevIN, series decomposition, and attention variants, into shared units that methods import, enabling shared maintenance; 263 methods reuse at least one unit.
Shared routines split data as configured, fit scaling on training data only, select checkpoints on validation data, and compute metrics consistently.

Agents use Compose to combine presets, Override to change settings, and Sweep to expand methods or values. For new-data benchmarking, an agent combines dataset and method presets, fixes the lookback, horizon, and training budget, and sweeps methods and seeds.

Recursive Improver brings external resources and agent-produced outcomes back into the shared workbench through checks for usability, complexity, and consistency (Fig. 2d). Failed checks prompt revision and rechecking before integration, supporting workbench maintenance.

review_audit.notes: The existing umbrella module duplicates the separately supported workbench components. Layer of knowledge-cards is a close call (cards describe forecasting methods and protocols); decided GTS because the card structure is task-neutral.

Forecast-specific content is resource content, not the mechanism; task membership does not decide scope.
Units such as RevIN and series decomposition are extracted into importable blocks with their own cards and maintained separately from the card catalogue.

history.title_checked: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
history.claim_summary: TSFLab is an agent-agnostic workbench for time series forecasting research: compatible coding agents share a forecasting research guide, layered knowledge cards for 323 methods, 93 datasets and 71 reusable units, a declarative experiment runner under shared protocols, and a recursive improver that verifies and merges new resources.
history.evaluation_summary: Paper reproduction (four papers x three attempts) and benchmarking on new data (eight methods x two datasets x three attempts) with Codex CLI against no workbench, TSLib, and TFB, repeated with Claude Code and a second Codex model; module ablations; and a method-development pilot on ETTh1 and Weather. Reported gains: 20-163% higher completion and 11-66% fewer fresh tokens per completed task; the pilot uses 32.8-73.6% fewer fresh tokens and 9.2-68.8% less development time.
corrections: Gains are relative to coding agents without a workbench or with TSLib/TFB under the authors' prompts, budgets, and review criteria.
The method-development pilot covers two datasets and is reported as a pilot study.
history.notes: Identity and method/evaluation passages checked against the arXiv v1 PDF; not an independent reproduction.

agent_claim_evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame TSFLab as a workbench that equips compatible coding agents and supports agent-driven research.

ts_specificity_reason: R3.2 GTS: cards organize temporal dataset and method properties such as frequency, protocols, and model parameters, while the retrieval structure is not bound to a forecasting output objective. Another time-series task can use the same catalog mechanism with different resources; R3.1 TSK is not met, and R3.3 GH misses the temporal metadata in its state.

R3.2 GTS: reusable units such as normalization, decomposition, and attention operate on temporal series structure, but do not encode a particular forecast output criterion. They do not themselves define the forecast objective required by R3.1 TSK; R3.3 GH would omit the temporal data constraints.
